title: UPS Cargo Plane and Copa Airlines Jet Collide on Miami Airport Taxiway
meta_title: UPS Cargo Plane and Copa Airlines Jet Collide on Miami Airport Taxiway
meta_description: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collided on a Miami International Airport taxiway, prompting a federal investigation and minor injuries.
discover_titles: UPS and Copa Airlines Jets Collide at Miami Airport
Federal Investigation Underway After Miami Airport Plane Collision
Two Injured After UPS and Copa Jets Collide on Taxiway
spot: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet carrying 172 people collided on a taxiway at Miami International Airport, resulting in two apparent minor injuries and a federal investigation.
content_html:
Key Developments

A ground collision occurred at Miami International Airport involving a UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737-800NG passenger jet. According to the Federal Aviation Administration, the wingtip of the Copa Airlines jet struck the nose of the UPS cargo plane at approximately 9 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 14.

The Copa flight had just arrived from Panama City, Panama, carrying 166 passengers and six crew members, and was taxiing toward the terminal. Meanwhile, the UPS cargo plane was preparing for departure to Bogota, Colombia. Air traffic controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way to the incoming Copa flight, according to FAA records. Air traffic control audio captured moments after the impact, with voices acknowledging that an aircraft had gone too far before the collision.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue and airport officials confirmed that airport paramedics evaluated two passengers for apparent minor injuries, though neither required hospitalization. Greg Chin, communications director at Miami International Airport, stated that incoming and outgoing flights were redirected to other taxiways, preventing any broader impact on airport operations.

Key Takeaways

  • Involved Aircraft: A UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737-800NG passenger jet collided at the intersection of two taxiways.
  • Injuries and Response: Two passengers aboard the Copa Airlines flight were evaluated for minor injuries by airport paramedics, and no hospital transport was needed.
  • Operations and Investigation: Airport operations continued without major disruption as flights were redirected, while the FAA initiated a formal investigation.

Why It Matters

Taxiway incursions and ground collisions are critical safety events monitored closely by aviation authorities. This incident at Miami International Airport highlights the complex coordination required by air traffic controllers and flight crews on busy airfield grounds. The subsequent federal investigation will seek to determine the exact sequence of events and communications that led to the intersection strike, ensuring that safety protocols are rigorously reviewed to prevent similar ground incidents in the future.
